principles.statement: Incremental additions layered on top of existing state — a new 'vX.Y Updates' CSS block appended below an older one, a new self-heal pass creating fresh records instead of confirming existing ones — accumulate silent duplication and drift over time unless each addition either reconciles with (replaces/removes) what it supersedes or genuinely confirms nothing already covers the same ground.
principles.rationale: The exact same underlying bug class surfaced twice independently in one session, in two completely different systems: `ui/src/App.css` had two full, separately-authored `.setup-wizard`/`.setup-container` rule blocks (an older one fully superseded by a newer one, ~168 dead lines never removed), and ZSEI's jurisdiction container store had 299 duplicate JurisdictionRuleSet containers from 9 restarts of a self-heal pass that never correctly detected what already existed (method 23). Neither was caused by carelessness in the addition itself — both additions were individually well-formed — the shared root cause is 'add without reconciling against what's already there.'

heuristics.name: Recognize the 'Layered Update Comment' Smell
heuristics.description: A comment like '/* Setup Wizard v0.4.0 Updates */' or a versioned block name appended below existing rules for the same component is a strong signal that an earlier version of the same rules may still exist elsewhere in the file, un-reconciled. Grep for the base selector names across the whole file whenever adding a new versioned/dated block for something that already has styling.
heuristics.when_to_apply: Adding new CSS (or similarly append-only config/rule structures) for a component that plausibly already has existing rules.
examples: Confirmed via grep that `.setup-wizard`/`.setup-container` etc. were defined twice in App.css, ~1300 lines apart — the newer block's own comment ('v0.4.0 Updates') was the tell that an older, un-reconciled version might still exist.

heuristics.name: Periodically Audit Self-Heal Systems for Real Duplicate Counts
heuristics.description: Any 'runs every boot, additive, idempotent' self-heal pattern (a genuinely good, established pattern in this codebase) still needs its OWN idempotency verified periodically by directly counting real persisted records against expected unique counts — the pattern being architecturally sound doesn't guarantee any specific implementation of the 'already exists' check is correct (see method 23).
heuristics.when_to_apply: Any system using the 'runs every boot, additive, idempotent, self-heals' pattern established this session for methodology/jurisdiction/pipeline registration.
examples: Direct container count (299 vs ~41 expected) caught what nine consecutive clean-looking boot logs did not.

decision_rules.condition: Adding a new incremental/versioned block of rules, config, or self-heal logic on top of an area that may already have prior coverage.
decision_rules.action: Before or immediately after adding, grep/search for the same logical keys (selector names, scope identifiers, dedup keys) elsewhere in the same file/store, and reconcile (remove the superseded original, or confirm the check that prevents duplication is itself durable per method 23) rather than leaving both to coexist indefinitely.
exceptions: The old and new blocks are genuinely both still needed (e.g. a real `@media`-scoped responsive override, not a full duplicate) — confirm this by checking whether removing the older one changes rendered behavior, not by assuming.
